title.narrative: Feed the Future Nigeria Integrated Agricultural Activity

description.narrative: (Nigeria): With FY 2022 funds, activity will:.Support the scale up of interventions in the current focus states of Adamawa and Borno and expand the community seed production into the additional states of Gombe and Yobe. These intervention will include: Identifying 2,250 seed producers to become Community Based Seed Entrepreneurs (CBSE) and Establishing 150 CBSE cooperatives consisting of a minimum of 15-20 members; Develop and roll out a profitable and sustainable seed production and supply system and design appropriate business models needed for CBSE to sell certified seeds to smallholder farmers in the local markets; and Promote good crop varieties and management practices that are best suited for each agro-ecology in the selected states. This activity will contribute to the economic recovery in Northeast Nigeria in the wake of the devastation caused by the ongoing insurgency in the region, focusing on supporting vulnerable populations disenfranchised by the conflict and seeking to re-engage them in basic farming activities. The activity promotes climate-smart agriculture that aims to increase agricultural productivity and strengthened capacity to withstand shocks and stresses, which include those that are as a result of climate change. This activity contributes to addressing the challenges and obstacles holding back the agricultural, health, and nutrition sectors through inclusive, gender-sensitive, and sustainable agricultural-led economic growth. The activity directly contributes to the Mission's FtF strategy as well as Goal 1 and 2 of the Joint Strategic Plan. The activity will promote bio fortified seeds (such as vitamin A fortified maize, zinc fortified rice, and iron fortified cowpea) to enable CBSE to cultivate bio fortified crops. Also the activity will facilitate diversification and increase production of nutrient-dense crops, including processing, storage, preservation, and market expansion for vulnerable groups, particularly for nutritious foods....
